name: ScreenshotOne
tagline: Managed API for rendering websites, HTML, and Markdown as images or PDFs

pricing.notes: $0.009 per successful screenshot beyond the included allowance. A free tier includes 100 screenshots per month.

verdictSummary: A competent coding agent can build a useful self-hosted screenshot endpoint around Playwright in a weekend. Matching ScreenshotOne's reliable browser fleet, proxy locations, stealth behavior, maintained blocking rules, videos, and production edge-case handling is a much larger infrastructure product.
coreLoopDIY: Send a URL or HTML to an authenticated HTTP endpoint and receive a cached PNG, JPEG, WebP, or PDF rendered by a local Chrome/Chromium worker.
requirements: a machine with enough memory to run Chrome/Chromium
whatYouLose: managed browser capacity, rate limiting, and high availability
maintained ad, cookie banner, chat widget, and popup blocking rules
residential proxies, selectable IP locations, and stealth tuning
scrolling screenshots, video generation, and GPU rendering
production support for difficult sites and browser edge cases
moatNotes: browser fleet, blocking-rule corpus, proxies, and rendering reliability
whyPeopleStillPay: They want a screenshot API that stays reliable across hostile, slow, dynamic, and consent-heavy sites without operating Chrome/Chromium workers, updating blocking rules, managing proxies, or debugging browser failures.
notes: The basic API is buildable; dependable rendering at scale and the maintained cleanup data are the paid product.
prompt:
Build a production-grade, self-hosted alternative to ScreenshotOne.
Requirements:

- Explore screenshotone.com and review its public documentation before designing the product.
- Rebuild the documented screenshot, PDF, HTML, Markdown, animation, and video rendering features.
- Use TypeScript, Node.js, Playwright, PostgreSQL, Redis-backed queues, and object storage.
- Design a scalable API, worker fleet, caching layer, webhooks, retries, and usage controls.
- Write a cookie banner blocker and an ads blocker with smart detection and bypass heuristics.
- Back the blockers with thousands of real-world tests, fixtures, and continuous evaluations.
- Handle difficult dynamic sites, lazy loading, popups, consent flows, browser failures, and rendering edge cases.
- Add authentication, signed requests, rate limits, audit logs, metrics, tracing, and operational dashboards.
- Package every service with Docker and provide local development through Docker Compose.
- Deploy the platform to Kubernetes with autoscaling, rolling updates, health checks, and resilient storage.
- Build a comprehensive automated test suite covering the API, browser workers, blockers, queues, and deployment.
- Include architecture documentation, API documentation, runbooks, security guidance, and deployment instructions.
- Do not call ScreenshotOne's API or depend on its private systems.
- Deliver a working end-to-end platform and demonstrate it against a broad evaluation set.
